overall: Los Angeles is deep in a classic June Gloom pattern, with overnight temps locked flat at 62.6°F under a persistent marine layer bringing patchy fog, mostly cloudy skies, and light SW onshore flow. Temperatures have shown zero velocity or acceleration since at least midnight PT, consistent with a well-established marine layer suppressing any overnight radiative variability. Active weather alerts in the region (Red Flag Warnings, Extreme Heat Warnings) are all confined to inland desert zones — Yuma, Imperial County, Las Vegas corridor — and carry no relevance to the coastal LA forecast today.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP model agreement is unusually tight: ECMWF 68.2°F, HRRR 69.8°F, NBM 67.0°F, all clustering within a 2.8°F spread and centering near the NWS point forecast of 69°F. The current running max of 62.6°F (~01:49 PT) is fully consistent with expected pre-dawn behavior under cloud cover — no anomalous warmth or cold is evident relative to model expectations.
max_temp_prediction: With fog forecast to clear by 11am PT and afternoon conditions trending partly-to-mostly cloudy, solar heating will be moderated but present. The 2–3 PM PT peak timing implied by NWP models is typical for coastal LA under these conditions. Model consensus and NWS guidance converge firmly on the 67–70°F corridor, with the bulk of probability mass in the 68–70°F range. The persistent SW onshore flow and slow marine layer erosion slightly favor the lower end of that range, suggesting a most-likely outcome near 68–69°F. Confidence is moderate-high given tight multi-model agreement; the main downside risk is slower fog clearance holding the high near 67°F, while the upside risk of an earlier-than-expected burn-off could push temps briefly toward 70°F.
